title: Why do repeated letters turn grey in word games?
practice: Try BrainiWord. When a letter repeats, compare all its tiles before choosing your next word.

sections.html: A grey duplicate means the answer has no further copy of that letter for that tile. Answers can repeat letters. One L can turn yellow while another turns grey, so read the whole row before ruling L out.
sections.title: Can the answer contain the same letter twice?

sections.html:
Hidden word: APPLE. Guess: ALLEY. This is a teaching example, not today’s answer.

  1. A: green. Right position.
  2. First L: yellow. Present, but in position four.
  3. Second L: grey. The only L is already accounted for.
  4. E: yellow. It belongs in position five.
  5. Y: grey. There is no Y.

Y is absent; the second L is an extra copy. Those grey tiles tell different stories.
sections.title: Try APPLE against ALLEY

sections.html:
Matching positions are checked first. With answer LEVEL and guess LEMON, L and E turn green. Both letters also appear elsewhere in LEVEL: green does not mean “no more copies”.

Answer APPLE, guess AMPLE: what happens to P?

It turns green in position three. The second P, in position two, is not tested by this guess.
sections.title: Why the green tiles take priority

sections.html:
After ALLEY, you know A is first, E is not fourth and the single L is neither second nor third. Y is absent.

Ask: “Where can it go?” and “How many copies fit?” For more clue spotting, try finding the link in a Connections puzzle.
sections.title: Use the clue in your next guess

sections.html:
BrainiWord allows five tries at a five-letter word. A guess must pass its English word-list check. A rejected word uses no attempt; if the check cannot connect, retry when the connection returns.

Similar games may use different word lists or limits. See how Daily and Anytime play differ.
sections.title: A quick note before you play BrainiWord

description: One L turns yellow; the other turns grey. A worked example explains what repeated letters tell you in a five-letter word puzzle.
